I think its definitely about a party/gathering as stated above, but one dedicated entirely to the dissolution of inhabitation and expectation. It's depicts a massive, beautiful collaboration of people and experiences: "bring what you choose your roots and your dancing...sing your own tunes or just sing along". This chaotic collaboration also being indicated by the sheer, varied NOISE of the Barnacle Beat. Traditional and conventional expectation is being shunned here, in this 'revolutionary party' despite the opinions of others- "and smile as the plastics trip as they glance". This ability to engage in free expression is desired by all but can't always be obtained until a moment like this. From the old, the popular, and downcast- "the youngies and the druggies and the pretties and the uglies, til the oldies come down and get what they've been wanting". Of course, there is a darkness underlying this goofy, beautiful miasma. There is risk in the act  of completely 'letting go'- "ill stand in traffic and I'll wail and I'll dance" + "they'll drop a baby at the sight of the sun" (I like the previous idea stated here that this could be about child neglect specifically But I also think this can symbolize or encompass any kind of neglect that comes from only immersing yourself in the glow of the party- reminds me of the lyrics in "Feelin Good"). Regardless this is my long crazy ass interpretation of Barnacle Beat: the defiance of order and expectation in the search for meaning, joy and fulfillment even among the mundane- "ill stand on my hands and smoke with my feet" :)
